abduction_trace.peirce_secondness: TWO LAYERS OF MASQUERADING: (1) SysInternals.exe mimics Microsoft SysInternals Suite via spoofed version info — legitimate SysInternals never uses URLDownloadToFileA or modifies system files. (2) vmtoolsIO.exe mimics VMware Tools — legitimate VMware components install to Program Files\VMware, not c:\Windows\, and are digitally signed. Hosts file redirection targets AV test domains (wicar.org, eicar.org), preventing security validation. Prefetch deletion destroys execution timeline. Habit incongruence: SysInternals.exe 6/6 anomalies (90%), vmtoolsIO.exe 4/4 anomalies (60%).
abduction_trace.peirce_thirdness: Complete malware kill chain with dual masquerading and multi-layer defense evasion: INITIAL ACCESS via social engineering (T1204.002 — user executes trojanized tool) -> DEFENSE EVASION (T1562.001 PowerShell Defender disable + T1036 dual masquerading) -> EXECUTION (secondary payload download from malware430.com) -> PERSISTENCE (T1543.003 VMwareIOHelperService auto-start) -> ANTI-FORENSICS (T1070.004 prefetch deletion + hosts file manipulation). The attacker weaponized trust in two legitimate brands (SysInternals, VMware) simultaneously. This is Carnegie Masquerading Legitimacy: borrowing authority from trusted entities to suppress analyst scrutiny.
